title: Technology Sector Update for 10/31/2018: CDW,FB,FEYE,DDD - Nasdaq.com
text:

Technology stocks continue to soaring in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding more than 2.7% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising over 1.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) CDW Corp ( CDW ) climbed almost 15% on Wednesday, reaching a best-ever $92.18 a share, after the technology consultants reported improved Q3 financial results compared with year-ago levels and also topping Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, CDW earned $1.42 per share, rising from $1.08 per share during the same quarter last year and and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.08 per share. Revenue increased to $4.37 billion from $3.93 billion last year and also exceeding the $4.24 billion analyst mean.
In other sector news:
(+) FireEye ( FEYE ) was climbing by double-digits, at one point Wednesday rising over 12%, after the cyber-security software firm reported non-GAAP Q3 net income of $0.06 per share, improving on a $0.02 per share net loss during the year-ago period and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.04 per share. Revenue grew 7% to $212 million and also topped the $208.5 million Street view.
(+) Facebook ( FB ) was climbing over 4% again, recovering from a mid-morning slump and retracing most of a % advance earlier Wednesday that followed the social network company reporting Q3 earnings of $1.76 per share, beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.32 per share. Revenue increased to $13.72 billion from $10.32 billion during the same quarter last year, roughly matching the $13.82 billion analyst mean.
(-) 3D Systems ( DDD ) plunged Wednesday, dropping as much as 26% in recent trade, after the 3-D printer company reported a $0.02 per share fiscal Q2 unadjusted profit, reversing a net loss of $0.20 during the same quarter last year but still trailing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.01 per share. Total revenue increased to $164.5 million from $152.9 million last year but also missed the $171.8 million analyst mean.
